Um you know we didn't have our post postseason meeting like we we typically have. So uh I would say if anything I was less involved this this year than years past. Uh, you know, there's no secret that the last several years didn't go the way we wanted to, and there's a lot of blame to go around for that, myself included. Uh, and so we're we're in a great spot this year. We brought in, like I said, great people and great players, and uh, you can feel the the the vibes of the the locker room. You know, the energy is elevated right now. Um, we have some veteran guys that can can come in and show the younger guys on defense what it takes, what it means to to be great every day. Um, and so that's, like I said, exciting to be a part of. >> Why did you How important was that piece of it, the to have established veterans on defense that can show the younger guys that you're also banking on what it looks like? And have you seen that already? >> Yeah, you see that already. You see that out of out of Brian Cook from day one, you can tell that he's going to set a standard in that room and make everybody live up to it and put pressure on everybody if they don't. And you know, we have Jonathan Allen and and Dexter and BJ and TJ in that defensive line room now um to push the younger guys. You have Miles and Shamar and Cashes and Boyer on on the edges. And so when you're four deep at every position on the D line, usually you're going to be a pretty good defense. Doesn't really matter what what's happening everywhere else. And then um you know, we have a lot of trust in the in the linebackers that we're that we're bringing back. Those guys have um taken in leadership roles this off seasonason. That's been exciting to see. we know they have the talent to do it and they just got to go >> With everything from, you know, the experience signings to, like you mentioned, you know, you still feeling ready to go at the end of the season with, you know, not playing the full year. Is there kind of a different feel coming into the building to to start this season, an added excitement for you or is it just, you know, normal year in year out? >> Yeah, you definitely feel it. You definitely feel the the excitement and the energy from a lot of different guys. you know, obviously the veteran guys that we brought in, but then the young guys who were eager and hungry to prove themselves as well. >> Why why didn't you all have the meeting at the end of the season? >> Um, the timing just didn't play out right. You know, we we talked a lot on the phone, uh, but just not the in person one this year. >> Was it intentional to kind of maybe pull back a little bit how you series? What was that? What was that fight for you? >> No, I'm not sure. I'm not sure that that's the case. Um, that's just kind of how it happened. Joe, you in the last couple of years have wondered maybe your entire career here have had question marks in front of you on the offensive line. You don't have that this year. How nice is it to come into the off season, have five guys in front of you that project to be all starters. How good of a feeling is that? >> Yeah, it's so beneficial at the beginning of the season when you have the reps of communication that we've had with those guys. A line is all about communicating, knowing where your help is, playing off with each other, and when you have five returning starters, number one, that have done that, number two, that have all the talent to go and make it happen, that's a great feeling for me. There's no question that we have to be better in the first couple games at at those positions. And um you know, the last half of last year, they were unbelievable. and we just have to carry that into first couple weeks of this year and and beyond. >> Is there anything you've learned over the last six or seven years about what it takes to have success in this league that you maybe didn't know coming in or in your first year or two in the league? >> Just about consistency, you know, how consistent can you be on a day-to-day basis? How consistent can you be every single Sunday putting yourself and your team in position to to try to win the game? Uh that starts with your routine, with your day-to-day process. You know, coaches tell you that when you're younger and you start to develop it, but until you're actually in it, you don't necessarily know how uh important that that process really is. >> Did you change anything, Joe, in in your off season preparedness to maximize your readiness to to come here and hit the ground running? Yeah, I tweak and change things every year depending on how how I felt the year before, how things went the year before, things that I think I can improve on. >> It seems like you did a ton um just kind of outside of football this offseason. Did you make it a point to maybe try to enjoy yourself a little bit more uh this offseason you had in previous years? What was that kind of like that work life balance split? >> I'm not sure I've done I did more than than the last couple years. It might just be a little more publicized now. You guys get to see a little more of it. Um, but certainly you have to find some happiness outside of football uh in the time that you have because you know I want to play this game a long time and it can't just be football all day every day. You have to find some some other places that you can find fulfillment. Uh especially as you get older, you know, you football can be 247 for a while. But you know what? As I'm closing in on 30, I got to find some some other places for that. >> Do you feel that lingering? >> I don't know yet. I don't know. I don't know if that's just day-to-day soreness or if that's just getting older. >> Feel the publicity as well as you do as you show up to to different events and stuff. Does it feel different? >> I mean, certainly. It's uh I'm getting used to it, though. It's not it's not anything new for me. And as I as I get older and and reflect on on that, I get more and more comfortable in in those positions. Obviously, it's never going to be normal. It's never going to feel normal, but um I'm getting better at handling it. >> Was there anybody involved in the flag football event? We were talking when we were at Arizona for league meets with Larry Fitzgerald. said like you were actually working the phones trying to like put it together. How did that all come together and how did you end up kind of so in involved in that part of it? >> Um well obviously I have a a good relationship with Michael at Fanatics and um and with Tom obviously and and flag football means a lot to to the league. you know, they're trying to push that internationally and obviously with the Olympics coming up. Um, they're trying to make that more and more popular and that's for me it's an exciting thing to be a part of trying to grow football whether it's flag or or tackle football and um I think one will go with the other. If one gets popular the other one will as well and I want to be a part of that. >> I mean what So when you're calling guys what's your pitch? What's your pitch? >> I'm not sure I was pitching anybody. I was more so just like, "Hey, are you playing?" Um, just trying to figure out who was who was going to be >> uh out there with me, you know. >> Yeah. You know, when you a lot of guys focus on themselves, their contracts, their football life. Obviously, being an ambassador for the game is sounds like it's been kind of important to you over the years. When did that become an important thing to you? Um, I would say ear earlyish in my career, the first couple years when you see how the league pushes certain teams and um puts certain teams in uh big spots, why they do what they do. Um, studying that and the teams that are in those positions year in and year out. Um, there's a reason for it and that's a position that I want the Bengals to be in. to to follow up on that. I believe it was Shawn Payeyton who said that after the flag football experience like he he maybe be surprised if a real NFL player ended up playing in the Olympics. You you said that you wanted to be a part of it. So, do you plan to be a part of the flag football in the Olympics after this experience? >> Yeah, we'll see. We'll see. Uh you know, timing is everything and uh you know those conversations kind of started this year, but you know, there's a long way to go until we get there. That's something that that I'd like to do depending on obviously timing and um how people here feel about it, but that that'll be a conversation for a later date. >> What are those conversations like with the team? Like how hard is that working that balance of what you can do something like that off the field versus obviously not wanting to feel like you're putting yourself at risk? >> Um those conversations are great. Uh you know, there were no qualms about me doing that, but if there were, then I wouldn't have done it. Um, so there's constant dialogue with Duke and Zach and and everybody about things that I want to do, things that um, maybe I should or shouldn't do. There's constant dialogue with them. >> Are they going to let you keep playing? Is that been a conversation? Are they or have they said, "Hey, we don't want you to do this moving forward, or are they still free?" >> U, we haven't talked about it since since the the game. >> Talk about the idea of trying to elevate the Bengals onto a bigger platform. uh during the course of your career. Do you think that the Bengals are in a better spot now than they were years ago? And how much more work is there to go in that? >> Definitely. I think the number one number one thing is you have to win and you know, we're going to go win a lot of games this year and play great and and win a Super Bowl and um you know, everything that comes with that comes with that. >> Part of that, too, is playing internationally. You've spoken in here before about your desire to do that. you're going to get that chance this year. What was your reaction when you found out you're going to Madrid? >> Yeah, it's exciting. Um not sure when we're going to go out yet, but it'll be exciting to experience that um in a predominantly soccer city. Um you know, I know some people that live out there, so they'll be able to come to the game and um you know, hopefully put on a show for everybody. >> There's something exciting about bringing the Bengals brand to that. You know, you talk about yourself, Jamar T, the exciting brand of football you guys play. Is that part of it too that excites you about taking that brand overseas? >> Definitely. That this, you know, we're in the entertainment business at the end of the day and, you know, I want to go and put on a show for the fans. I'm every single time that I step foot on the on the field and having new platforms and new places to do that is exciting for us. >> Do you know any of the uh Madrid athletic players? >> I do. Yeah, >> a lot of focus has been on the defensive additions this year, but for you personally, how significant was getting Flaco back? >> Yeah, it's exciting. You know, I love being around Joe and and watching him play. Um, and knowing that I have somebody behind me that can come in and step in the way that he did last year is, uh, I think we'll put our team in a good position. >> Are you surprised he didn't get a starting job? Yeah, I would say based on the way he played, I was surprised nobody wanted that to happen. What would I Did I say would I say I was surprised? Um I was surprised based on the way he played last year. Yeah, for sure. conversations with him part of that work life balance approaching 30 kind of the re focusing on on that type of thing. >> No, not necessarily. That's kind of um kind of realized that on my own. >> You um you talked last year about the carbon fiber plate in your foot or in your shoe. Is that a thing of the past or is that something you'll continue? >> We'll see. It won't be as stiff. I'll definitely wear wear something this year. Um, yeah, we'll we'll see where that goes. I'm trying a lot of different things out right now to to figure out what what works best for me right now, but it definitely won't be as stiff as it was last year. >> Just preventative wearing moving forward. >> Yeah. Yeah. Why not? Yeah. >> Last time we talked to you, you said that you were going to evaluate everything as far as your offseason program, what you do as far as finding ways that you can to stay on the field more. Obviously, with so many of your injuries being flukes, did you did anything come to light this off season that that you're going to change or was there a conversation you had with someone that that helped you or inspired you or are you pretty much keeping everything the same? No, I definitely changed some things in my training. Um, you know, my mindset changes every year. You know, you have to grow and adapt in this league if you want to continue to get better. And um, that's what we did. >> What did you change? >> I'll keep that to myself. >> Is there anybody you met at the Met that was uh, you know, kind of wow and maybe got a new number in your phone that >> No, I'm not. I think I think the WOW is kind of out of my out of my realm these days. I've been around, done a lot of things, but uh I got to see my friend Mondo, who I went to college with, who uh he he's the one that breaks all the pole vaulting world records. Feels like every day or every weekend that he goes and does it. So, it was great to see him. You know, I hadn't seen seen him in a while. >> What do you think? Do you think you're winging people? Is it is it on the other end now that you're winging somebody? >> I don't know. I don't I'm sure the young I'm sure the youngsters. Yeah, I'm sure the youngsters. >> You're still 29, Joe. So, >> I'm still 29, I guess. Yeah. >> You have a favorite offseason event that you want to do or or like is there something that >> I always just enjoy hanging out with my friends. Doesn't really matter >> where it's at. Just seeing seeing old friends. >> Last year you uh made it a point that you wanted to play Baltimore in the jungle here in Cincinnati. Now, you do get that after a 4-year prime time out there. Um, looking at the schedule in general, is that kind of the one that you have circled other than maybe Madrid? >> Yeah, circled. I'm not, you know, anytime we play the Ravens, that that one is circled. Um, you know, that that that goes back years back when back from when Lamar and I were a lot younger. So that's always a battle when we when we get after it, you know, Madrid into Sunday night into Monday night. That's going to be a tough stretch for us going um overseas and then coming back and playing Steelers on Sunday night and then playing Commanders on Monday night. That'll be tough. >> You does it give you any extra juice knowing that Trey will be coming back for that game as well? >> Yeah, that'll definitely be fun. That'll definitely be fun. >> What' you think when you saw the news that he was signing there? not very surprising. >> Why is that? >> Because I know Trey. I love Trey and um I just know how he how he operates. >> What about playing uh Pat after I think it's been three years since you played him? You get that chance now here back in Cincinnati? Yeah, hopefully, you know, we're both going to be in different spots than we were last year. I think, you know, we're gonna have a really good team. Obviously, I think they'll they'll have a really good team and, you know, we play them, I think, week 14 or 15. Um, so that'll be one that leading up to the playoffs. Hopefully, hopefully we get two shots at them. >> That's also circle. >> Yeah, >> we've we've asked Zach this a number of times, but just curious your perspective on this. You guys are the only team in the division that didn't undergo a head coaching change and a whole coaching staff turnover. Do you think that could be used as an advantage for you guys heading into the season? >> Yeah, there's there's positives and negatives for um for us, you know, if you you know, you play them early in the year, you're not necessarily super dialed on what they're going to be doing. Um, I don't think we have trying to think of when our first divisional game is. >> Third week. >> Yeah. So, you have we got two weeks to uh dial in on the stuff that they're going to be doing. Um, it's a lot tougher if you plan a new head coach or new defensive coordinator week one or week two when there's just not enough tape to really be super confident in what they're going to try to do against you. But um with with a couple weeks under our belt, I think um that gives us a little more of an advantage than had we played them a couple weeks earlier >> after the season finale. If I would have told you you guys would make the offseason additions that you made, what do you think your reaction would have been? >> Yeah, I'd be fired up. Um like I said, I'm fired up about the people that we brought in. I'm fired up about the mindset guys are bringing on on the daily. Uh, I'm fired up about the energy everybody is bringing in the weight room and conditioning and practice. Obviously, we're not going against each other yet, but when OTAA start, I'm excited to get some competition going. Um, so we have a lot a lot of work to get done before July, before September, but you know, I love where we're at right now. >> What is so valuable to you about being here this time of year? And what is what can you most get out of it? >> Number one is just getting around the guys, building the camaraderie in the locker room. Uh number two, there's just, you know, it's hard to replace just being on the field, being in the in the building for as long as we are, going from lifting to practice to running. You can do all that all all you want by yourself, but it's just a little different when you're out there practicing for for an hour and a half and then you're conditioning and you're lifting before that. Uh just feels different on your legs. So getting your legs used to football activities is beneficial. Do you have any offensive uh milestones, I mean, as a team, maybe as an individual that stats that you're looking to you got to do this year, you think in order to be successful offensively? >> Yeah, we got to be more explosive. I think, you know, we've been great in in third down and in red zone situations, but um we got to get back to being the explosive offense that we were, you know, in 21 and 22. Um, you know, for a couple years there, teams are playing us a little differently. So, we had to adapt and now defenses are starting to turn back the other way where they're pressuring more. They're playing a little more man. So, we have to go back to burning them and and becoming an an explosive offense again. >> There any stats that any individual stats that kind of you're looking at after an offseason? >> Um, I'm pretty close to Bengals franchise touchdown record. I think I'm like 50 or something away. So, that'd be nice to break this year. >> You care about an MVP. >> You always want to be MVP of the league, Super Bowl MVP, win a Super Bowl. You know, all those things are I'm not necessarily sure I'd say a seasonal goal of mine would be to do that because you never know how um things will play out as far as winning the MVP. A lot of things have to go right, but um I'd like to win one eventually for sure. I >> mean, you saw what this roster looked like in 2021, albeit you were young, but that was a Super Bowl roster. Do you think what you see right now from this organization and in that locker room is a Super Bowl roster. >> I think this is the most talented roster that we've had since I've been here. >> 47 away, 48 from breaking. >> Doable. >> Thanks, Joe. >> Thanks. Do I?

title: Dan Hoard interviews Dexter Lawrence II and B.J. Hill
text: I'm Dan Hoard with best buds and reunited teammates B.J. Hill and Dexter Lawrence. By the way, in case you're wondering why I'm wearing a sling, I challenged sexy Dexy to an arm wrestling contest and lost. Just kidding. Let me start with this question. What is it about the other guy that you like and respect so much? Dexter, you go first. >> Um, really just this is personality. You know, you ask anybody around the building, you know, he's a guy that gets along with anybody, but he's true to himself always and and I can respect that a lot. B.J.? Mine Mine is more like off the field, like to see who he is as a man. Um, like he always has your back no matter what. Um, he's a guy who who who cares about his brother. He's always going to take care of his brother and always be there for you. All right, I'm going to turn the clock back approximately 11 years. Dexter Lawrence, five-star recruit, number two recruit in the country, goes on a visit to NC State and B.J. Hill is picked to be the guy to host. What do you guys remember about that first meeting? B.J., you're up >> It was actually more than one person. It wasn't just me. We had like 10 guys [laughter] there, coaches. I think we went to um Dave & Buster's, I believe, or something like that or Topgolf or we just sit there and have a good time and, you know, it just didn't work out. >> [laughter] >> B.J. did a good job, I assume, along with those other teammates. >> Yeah, I remember them, for sure. >> I remember them, but uh you know, just it was I'm for me, I feel like that's kind of where we kind of connected. He he say the Giants, but for me it was it was on that visit. You're both North Carolina guys. You're from Wake Forest, you're from Oakboro, is it? Similar towns? Uh, probably similar. Wake Forest probably growed up grew up a little bit. Mine is Mine is way smaller than Wake Forest, for sure. Way smaller. So, you considered NC State. You obviously chose to go to Clemson. In your first year at Clemson, your teams played each other. Clemson was heavily favored in Death Valley. You guys almost pulled off the upset. You missed an easy field goal with like 2 seconds to go. Clemson won the game in overtime. Does that one still hurt? That one still [laughter] hurt. That one That one would have changed a lot, you know, for our program. We would have won that game for sure, but you know, it is what it is. And does that one still rank among your favorites? >> Yeah, all I remember was laying on the ground and the crowd roaring. Like I'm like, "What's going on?" Then they get up and he misses and and we we just took advantage of it after that. Did you guys maintain a friendship while you were in college playing at different places, or did it rekindle when you were both with the Giants? I think it rekindled at the Giants. Yeah, cuz we wasn't messing with NC State. >> They didn't like us. We didn't like them, so it was cool. So, you got drafted by the Giants and then 1 year later, you were selected by the Giants. You're in New York City, two North Carolina guys in the Big Apple. Did that help that bond get stronger? I think so. Like I think Like just like Like we kind of we kind of knew each other, so that made it the For me, that made the transition easy. Just like here, like we know each other, so this transition has been pretty smooth for me. Um but yeah, I say at the Giants, that's where it kind of rekindled and it it ain't going to slow down. New York City can be a little bit intimidating when you're not from there. Did you help him adapt? Yeah, it was it was good. It was a good transition especially for me coming from a small town. Didn't know much about big cities or anything like that, only Raleigh, North Carolina. Um but it was kind of a easy transition because for one, all I did was focus on football, same with him. We're all about ball. All we used to want to win and play good on the defensive line. So, we really kept the outside noise on the outside and did what we had to do on the field. So, when you're teammates there together in New York, you got to see the other guy on the field first hand. What do you respect about each other's game? You talked about the off-field stuff earlier, but how about the on-field stuff? I I think his approach to the game, he's real he's real consistent. Like you you know what his routine's going to be. You know like his mindset going into the game and you know that he's going to do his job and you just got to do yours. So like I just I like his approach like and and that kind of like what was molding me like like he's like my my vet kind of. So like watching his approach go out to practice early and go through his routines and you know it ain't changed. So That's all I respect. And the on >> And the on-field stuff from your perspective. >> with him. The way he approached the game, the way he dominates games and like he he attacks the games or even practice like he don't know anything He asks questions like he don't know anything. So you love seeing guys who year eight, year whatever asking questions going out there in practice giving their all and not just you know taking it easy um cuz you can get complacent in the game especially the longer you play, but he attacks each and every day if if it's practice, workouts, um games, um at a high level and you you love to see that. So you're teammates in New York for a few years and then B.J. got traded to Cincinnati just before the 2021 season. Were you heartbroken? >> Yeah, that was tough. That was tough. And and the yeah how it went down was tough. Um I ain't believe him at first. >> I was trying to fight it, but you know I think I think you know for my like just to be honest like I think everything happens for a reason and I think you know me watching that and then talking to him almost every >> every day he was here. Um you know kind of just and now we're now we're back together and it's it's it's time to take advantage of it, you know? Like I told him like when I first got here he said we not we not going to waste this moment. So that's what that's what it's about. The trade worked out well for you right off the bat. The Bengals went to the Super Bowl that first year, but were you sad that your buddy was left behind in New York? Yeah, for sure. Um just like I said this is the way it went and all went down. Um, probably I probably had one of my best camps I've ever had there. Just giving all I got just to give myself a chance to get on the field there and it just didn't work out. Um, leaving some of your best friends is is sucks, especially when you've been there for shoot, almost four years. You're almost there for four years. Um, because it sucked. But, you know, like you said, everything happens for a reason. I'm here for a reason and that's to win games. What was the Bengals Super Bowl run like for you watching B.J.? So, like so I I I wasn't I didn't My rookie year I didn't watch too much of them until the playoffs started and I was like, he's really about to do this. >> He's really about to do this. And then he's talking junk talking junk all day every day. >> And then they get there and I'm like, wow, he he made it to the Super Bowl and I was happy. I was I was You ask like my wife, you can ask her. I was just in the in the living room just cheesing and smiling the whole time. Just happy, you know, for him and his success early success of being traded. So, this year after seven years in New York, you decided to seek a trade. Did you reach out to B.J. for advice? Um, I did. I did. Um, I did and you know, I'll say it was a little biased, but like I kind [laughter] of understood where he was coming from cuz we just talked a lot and I kind of understood, you know, how the how the Bengals were and how they how they ran things around here. So, it's it's it's been smooth and I think, you know, his influence helped a little bit. [laughter] B.J., on behalf of all of us, thank you. >> What did you say to help sell it? I just told him the truth. That's how I As me as a man, as a brother, like I just got to tell him the truth what I thought about the organization, teammates, like just everybody. And he made a decision. So, it came down the news came down on a Saturday night. The night before you two guys were together for B.J.'s early birthday party. Did you have an inkling? Did Did you know it was going going the next day? Uh, slightly, but on my end I I didn't truly know, you know, so I always had to be like, you know, I couldn't fully commit until I fully fully knew it, but at the at the back of my mind I was kind of I kind of understand what was going on behind the scenes and, you know, when it came to fruition I I had to jump. We've learned since that it was in the works for a couple of weeks or at least the Bengals were trying to get something done for a couple of weeks. Did they ask you what kind of guy is he? Is this something we need to do? I would I didn't know anything about it, okay? [laughter] I didn't know anything about it until everybody else knew about it, you know what I'm saying? But, um, you know, like I said, I just had we had a great conversation with some guys. Um, and of course you want a great guy like like Dex in your locker room who's good on the field off the field, good with other people, get along with other people. Um, so you want a guy like that in your locker room. So, there's nothing bad bad to say about him. What have these first few weeks been like together here in Cincinnati? It's for me it's been it's been good cuz now like, you know, I I I learned a lot in New York, but now I'm like, you know, I'm picking up on some of his habits, you know, to help me grow as a as a player and a man. So, I think that this transition, you know, has just been what what was what was bound to happen, man. What's been special for you? Uh, just having him around the building. I feel like just having him here added at least two or three more years on on on [laughter] my career. Um, yeah. So, like I'm all smiles. I like I said, I literally have nothing bad about to say say about Dex, man. You you like I said, you love to have people in the building like him. Make your for one make your job easier and the guy who's going to help lead this group and, um, just a great teammate. Um, you love you love guys like that. He's the godfather of your kids, correct? >> Yeah. I mean, really that's about the highest compliment you can pay to somebody in all seriousness. >> Yeah. No, that was a that was a true honor. That was a true honor. Um and you know, I got to I got a boy, you know. >> That's true. But it was when when they called us, we couldn't we couldn't turn that down. All right, I want to play a little game I call know your best bud. I'm going to ask you five questions about the other guy, see how well you know your friend. All right, we know your current numbers. B.J. wears 92, you wear 97. Do you know the other guy's college number? What did B.J. wear at NC State? Ooh, 90 98. Boom. >> Well done. Okay. Well done. What did Dexter wear at Clemson? >> 90. 90. All right. Let's let's take it back a step further. Both of your high school numbers were retired. What did B.J. wear at West Stanley? >> I literally went to the retirement. Uh It was a little dude number. I can't remember. >> Single single digit. Uh five? >> Five. [laughter] Do you know what he wore at Wake Forest High? Yeah, it was offensive line. Correct. [laughter] 76. >> 71. >> [screaming] [laughter] >> ALL RIGHT, DEXTER HAS TAKEN THE LEAD. Do you know the other guy's like high school team name? The the West Stanley what's? Ooh, that's a good one. Um uh this sounds like it flows, Lions. >> It kind of flows, but it's the Colts. >> Colts. Okay. Okay. >> The Wake Forest what's? Rebels. >> I don't know that one. Cougars. Cougars. Cougars. All right. That That was a tough one. >> That was a tough one. Okay. Each of you guys has interceptions in the NFL. B.J. actually has three, two in the regular season, one in the postseason. Dexter has one, but it was last year, so it's fresh on your mind. Can you name a quarterback that the other guy has picked off? [laughter] Uh I It was a home game, too, I think. I can't I can't I can't remember the quarterback, though. That was Nick Mullens, I think. Was that the Vikings game, B.J.? Yeah. Yeah. Kind of can you take us through kind of where where the team's frame is? >> Um, we we all, you know, again, it's a new team. Everyone's kind of been um in other spaces, you know, and and other teams. Um, but right now we're you finding our identity. We're coming together and getting getting work in each day. Um, so that's that's all part of development. You talked a little bit about Kirk. Um just watching him today, the passion and energy that he has is is pretty evident. Just like what does that do for the team and what has his impact been on the team so far? >> Um I think it's uh he's very direct. Um and uh I think that delivers that delivers a response to someone, you know, when someone says something. Um you know, uh the way he says it, you know, it's like, oh, all right, like let's go snap in. Um and uh you know, he's he's very on top of it. Um, you know, it's it's uh you know, you know, fires you up, you know, a little bit. Um, but no, he's been great. >> We talk about the different scheme when you guys don't have pads on, it's non-cont. Is it harder to implement those changes at this time of year than than say training camp when you would have that option? >> Um, yeah, training camp is ideal for hitting um and and you know, really finding you know, that's that's where the real competition um starts, but um OTAAS's, you know, you got to walk before you can run. you know, you gota you gota be in the right spots, all that. Um, so, uh, again, it's just mastering this process and just trying to get as much as we can out of the day.

title: Klint Kubiak: ‘We’re Off to a Solid Start'
text: What have you seen in the rel relationship between uh Kirk and Fernando? How's that been so far? >> Yeah, uh it's it's been it's been solid. You know, coach Janoko and coach Sully do a great job in that room. Um but two really competitive guys. Um you know, been really pleased with with their work ethic. Uh Aiden has been phenomenal. Can't say enough great things about him. >> Even from rookie camp, you can see the progression from Fernando at under center. Do you feel like he's starting to play a little more out of his head? >> Yeah, I think anything anything that you put in front of him, he's going to attack it, you know, so anything that's new, he spends extra time on it. You can tell he fixes things from uh from one day to the next. Uh very coachable. Uh and that could be said for uh for all those quarterbacks in the room. >> Hey Clint, there was a moment after stretching where the team got together and everybody was giving other high fives and kind of, you know, sharing some camaraderie. Was that an organic thing or did you guys did you build that into post stretching? >> I put that on our our our team leaders. You know, that's important for them to, you know, just come together before practice. I thought it was a little too l lengthy. You know, we probably lost two minutes of practice time right there. So, we can dap it up a little quicker next time. >> What is your approach to OTAAS? >> Uh to get these guys in position for training camp, get them in football shape for training camp. Um, obviously we're going to evaluate them, but you know, OTAAS puts you in position for training camp and then training camp puts them in position for the season. >> I know that process, but >> Colt Miller just being on the field. >> I know you haven't coached him yet, but how important is that just to see him out there participating? >> Yeah, very important. And our training staff done a phenomenal job of progressing him and uh, you know, he's running with the ones today. He's getting getting quality reps and I think, you know, he's ahead of schedule. He's a he's a competitive guy. Really counting on him this year. >> You mentioned you mentioned getting the guys ready for training camp. How much progression have you seen from Jamal McCoy in in rookie camp to where he is right now? >> Yeah, he's he's been excellent. He's he's come in here and worked his tail off, you know, doing everything that we've asked him to do. Um, you know, he's got out there on the practice field and and has shown the player that we've seen on tape. So, just looking forward to progressing him along with all those new DBs. You know, it's an impressive group. Really well coached group by by Joe and Matt and Robbie. Very competitive young men right now in that defensive back room. >> What is the plan with Jamal just in terms of managing what the health situation is? I mean, are you guys comfortable with him just going full speed at practice right now or where I guess what is the process there? >> Yeah, I think Alex Guerrero has a has a great plan for him as far as how many how many yards we give them a day, the rest that we give them, uh the time on the field as opposed to the turf. Um, you know, uh, but the great thing about about Germad thus far is he's responded really well. >> We saw Max Crosby out there stretching with the team. I was wondering, uh, where is he at in the recovery process and does the team still anticipate him to be ready by training camp? >> Yeah, we do. That's the goal. That's the goal. He's he's still the first one in this building every day working. uh he's a leader on our team and uh when he's out there you feel his presence and yes, we're counting on him being there for training camp and uh you know I wouldn't be surprised if Max was ahead of schedule. >> How important was it that he was out there though stretching and going through it with his guys? >> Yeah, that's just in his DNA. You know, you didn't have to ask him to do that. He's going to be there as much as possible and he knows that that we're counting on him to be a leader. So, um you know, he's he's showing his face, but he's also very engaged in the meetings and he's one of those guys you got to say woe to. you got to pull him back. He might jump in there in team period if you're not watching. You know, he's that competitive. Um really fired up to be uh get to coach him. >> How hard is it to take pressure off Ashton, especially if Mike can produce this year? >> Uh we want to put a lot of pressure on Ashton, you know, the the next guy that steps up, whoever that may be. That's going to be to be seen here in practice, OTAAS, in training camp. But um you know, we think we think we should continue to challenge Ashton and get more out of him. I mean, as from a durability standpoint, the load is this coach on him. >> Yeah. Uh, you know, I said that before. I think it's important to have have a quality second back, but you know, uh, the best players got to play and we got to get them on the field as much as we can. You know, I don't know the the play snap percentage, but you look at Christian McCaffrey, his his play snap percentage is high. So, those great backs, uh, they don't want to come off the field. You saw the passion that Kirk plays with out on the field, moving guys around, getting them in the right spots and also getting hyped up after that first down. What has his leadership and kind of energy brought to this team? >> Yeah, he's a professional. You know, he's he's played a lot of football. Uh he's a he's a leader that we're counting on right now. You know, you see that that side of him when it gets competitive. That was fun to get that move the ball period and get guys off of scripts and see how they respond and uh you know, you see the fire come out and that's what I want from our guys. just talking about Ashton, but a lot of those second year players on the team like Ashton, Jack B, Dante, big parts of those offense. How important is it to make sure that they have a second year lead going into this next year for the offense? >> Yeah, we're we're counting on them. You know, we're counting on them to to produce for us. The good thing is there's competition, you know, with Bes and, you know, with DT, there's a lot of competition in that receiver room and uh may the best man win. >> What have you noticed from Tyler Linderbomb so far at commanding the line? Uh just a quiet confidence, you know, just a uh a man out there elite running the show. Very athletic player, but a growing man. >> Coach's step brother's not in the schedule release. What were your thoughts on the acting skills of Fernando and Kurt? >> Yeah, I'd love for him to focus on football more. >> Rob Rob is a first time defensive coordinator. You're a first- time head coach. How much influence input will you have uh on the defensive side of the ball here, especially in OTAAS? >> Yeah. No, we're working together. we're we're, you know, teaming up on these installs. But, uh, you know, Rob's running the show. You know, he's he's done a great job. He's got a lot of, you know, talented assistants, you know, with Joe Woods. And, you know, there's some veteran coaches on there that are doing a great job. And, uh, we're going to we're going to put Coach Robbie in positions to call, you know, to call it periods here in OTAAS and in training camp so that, uh, he's ready to go come the season. >> What's been your impressions of Fernando Mendoza thus far? the way he's been trying to pick up uh the offense >> uh as advertised. You know, he he is not disappointed. He's working his tail off. It's very important to him. Asks a lot of great questions when he gets on the field. He's no BS. Um he's all ball. >> Is there anything that you've learned through this OTA's process about being a head coach and kind of taking that step back and take taking control of the entire team rather than just the >> Yeah. Um obviously learning that on the fly. Um, just we hired these these assistants for a reason. So, got to trust them to do their jobs and uh, you know, I know the Raiders brought me here for a reason as well, you know, uh, to coach offense. So, I'm going to be spending a lot of time with the offense and got to make sure I get that right. All the while being with the whole team. But, uh, Robbie Leonard and Joe D. Camilis, you know, two phenomenal coaches that I'm really happy to have leading their units. >> What is Terra Johnson status and also didn't see out there today either? Yeah, it's shoot, it's a voluntary time of year. Can't wait to get those guys back. Really fired up for the guys that are here. Um, but uh, you know, been in contact with both of those guys and and, uh, you know, they've been doing a great job. Some here, some away. >> What are the signs that you'll see that Fernando is making progress, that he's making the strides you want him to to make? >> Completions, you know, getting the ball to the playmakers and letting them work on time. That's that's the progress we want to see. Speaking of playmakers, playing, one of the guys you talked about early on when you took the job was Trey Tucker. What have you seen from him now that you guys have actually been on the field a little bit? >> Uh, really no surprise there from what you've seen previously. You know, he can run all day. Uh, he's a he's a quiet leader, a guy that u that we're going to put in a leadership role. You know, he's got to be a playmaker for us and he has been. And now let's go see what else we can get out of him. >> I know you don't want to make comparisons, but does he remind you of somebody you may have coached in the past with his skill set? >> Um, I Yes. It's not I sometimes that's not fair to say out loud. Um but when you got a guy that's that size and that competitive and works that hard, um there's not a whole lot of humans on the planet that can put as many yards on the field at that high of a speed. So, he's been really impressive. >> Being a part of your first draft as a head coach, how rewarding is it to kind of see those pieces come to life on the field? >> Yeah, really fun to get all these these young bucks in here. Um, I think I can't say enough great things about what what John Spyac has done for this roster. You know, and I think about the type of people that he's brought in. You know, there we're not out there coaching effort right now. We're not out there coaching accountability. Uh, we drafted we drafted that part and you it's hard to coach those things. You stress them every day. But, um, those guys really love football and now they're going to be in position to play fast. So, look forward to seeing their development. >> Zoom. Trey Zoom was playing a lot of right tackle today. Is that the position that you all see him playing at going forward or is it going to be moving around a little bit more? >> Yeah, really drafted Trey to be be able to play a lot of positions. So whether it's tackle, guard, center, he's learning it all. He's got uh he's got everything between the ears to do that and so we're going to give him chance to help us on all areas of the line. How how pleased or I guess just how would you evaluate the process that you've had of just installing everything you want to install offensively, defensively, what you wanted the practice to look like, film sessions, that sort of thing. Where are you at in just kind of evaluating that process? >> Yeah. Well, really never please. Really, we can always be better. We're always, you know, very critical of ourselves with how can we get the most out of these every hour for these players in a positive way and let them know that we are not wasting their time. you know, we we've put in the work for them to give them productive days. So, I think you're always trying to improve there. Um, we're off to a solid start. Everyone's undefeated right now, right? Um, but we know sooner or later that it's going to get real competitive and we got to find out, you know, who's the guys we can count on in those stressful situations, coaches included. >> I know it's I know it's early in the process, but how do you earn your shield? >> How do you earn your shield? Um, well, we'll find out if we get it by training camp. If we can uphold the standard that we've put in front of these players in our team meeting, you know, of uh if our conditioning level is where it needs to be, if we can practice the right way, if we can handle our business outside of the building, uh we can represent the shield the right way, then we'll put it back on. >> Seeing him up close now, >> who's that? Brock Bowers up close. >> Um he's kind of a football robot in a good way. He's a football robot from heaven. You know, he's a Cadillac out there. We got to get the most out of Brock, you know, whether wherever he goes, he's been successful in college and high school, whatever, whoever's coached him. Um, so, uh, you know, just can't say enough great things about him. Love his work ethic. He is a standard bear. >> Stukes, his versatility in the secondary, uh, what kind of key piece is he going to be? >> You said Stokes. Um, yeah, that's that's why we drafted him. very summer to Trey Zun, a guy that can play a lot of spots, a guy that has a leadership and uh those are all the things he did in college, but now he's got to go show it at this level. He's off to a good start and uh you know, he's got some really really talented coaches that are leading him. Um but I can't you know, when when he walks out there, he's dialed in. He knows what to do and uh he's a guy that just kind of finds his way around the ball. >> Just to clarify on the on the shield thing, it sounds like you're talking more of a team thing that it's not like individuals get it one at a time. >> Correct. Yes. Any more guys? Thanks. >> Thank you.

title: Zion Johnson Press Conference | May 20th, 2026
text: How would you sort of describe the adjustment now that you guys are on the field and you're in the meeting rooms and >> what's that transition been like for you in terms of learning a new offense kind of, you know, how do you sort of go about that process of kind of absorbing a new playbook? >> Um, it's been exciting. Uh this is the real step, you know, getting to, you know, put our offense against a really good defense, you know, that's good at disrupting and um you know, I think dayto-day we just work to improve our communication, our execution, uh our knowledge of the playbook. Um so yeah, I think it's been great. Um you know, these first two days we've had some things that we've seen that like, okay, we need to improve these things and we've seen some things that were like, oh, these are some good things that we have going for ourselves. So, um, you know, it's been a great two days. I think >> I know the real tests will come when the pads come on, but right now, what are the keys that you feel like are important that you guys take away from from these sessions here? >> Uh, execution, assignment, technique. Um, yeah, those are really the big three things. Uh, being locked in on what your assignment is on the play. You know, that means studying the playbook, knowing, you know, everything about your assignment. um technique, you know, we had a lot of times to nail down on the fundamentals and technique. So, seeing those things applied when somebody's in front of you as well. And then the last thing is just execution, like do you know the snap count? Do you know um you know what this play means? Uh what your assignment is on this play. So, >> how how do you think that's played out so far on the field for you guys? >> Um I think there's been some good. There's been some definitely things that aren't as good. Um but every day we look to improve. We look to hit the film and see where we can improve. And um we've got a lot of guys uh on offense in our room um in all the rooms, wide receiver room, quarterback room, running back room, tight ends that you know want to get better and are out here after doing work out here before doing work. Um so you know I feel great about you know us improving dayto day >> over the next over the next four months. What's your role in helping a rookie left tackle get used to the NFL? >> I mean I'm just here for whatever he needs. Um you know if he needs advice um you know I've got that. If if he needs experience, I've got that. You know, if he even wants to talk to, you know, somebody who's been in his shoes and, you know, can give him better advice than I can, you know, I'm willing to give that to him as well. Any really anything that that he needs. >> Off of that, what have you, how much has he sort of leaned into the the group here as a resource and as he's trying to get adjusted obviously to the NFL over the last month? >> No, he's awesome. I mean, he's a he's a sponge. Like, he's always asking questions like, "What could I do better here?" you know, questions in terms of his routine, like what should I be doing before practice? What should I be doing before list? Um, you know, I just think it's a awesome to be around a rookie that, you know, just has that thirst for knowledge and wants to get better. >> Dian, what about um just getting to see Elton out here after he's had to battle back from his injury and what's it like playing next to him just given the fact he obviously has so much experience at guard as well and he's probably somebody's brain you can pick, I would guess. >> No, absolutely. He's definitely a guy's brain I could pick, but you know, he has a lot of experience. uh has played at a high level, played on some good teams. So, uh he's a great resource for not just me, but everybody on our offensive line. >> Seems like >> Seems like Todd is determined to use every minute he can out on this practice field, keep you guys out of here [clears throat] for a long time. >> Yeah. Yeah. >> What kind of tone does that set for, for this football team? >> I mean, I think it's great. You know, you don't want the first time as a offense you, you know, encounter something that's problematic or something that's tough to be in camp. you know, for a player, you know, you get a chance to experience it on the field here, so you have like some reference to go back to during camp. So, I think it's great from the experience point of view for a player, but you know, the more we can work, the more we can, you know, work on our fundamentals and technique, I think the better. >> When they signed uh you and it seemed like there was some uncertainty on which positions you guys would be, but is it let's say now you're settled in at left guard, etc. confident is that for the progress of this team? >> I mean, I think it's great. I mean, honestly, the way I look at it, the way Elton looks at it, you know, we'll play whatever the team needs us to. Um, but, you know, right now, you know, they wanted me at left guard, they want him at center. If that were to change down the line, you know, we're going to do whatever we can to help the team win. So, >> seems like you guys have a lot of athletes and you were a really good athlete coming out of Boston College and everything. How do you contrast sort of the the offense with the Chargers to what you're doing now and how does that sort of fit you? >> Um I think you know there's a lot of opportunities to really you know show my athleticism. A lot of plays where I get to pull a lot of plays where you know I get to go out and run. Um so it's very exciting for me but I think it's a great system for our offensive line as a whole. Like you know not including myself like we have a lot of other guys that are athletic as well like Fondo really good athlete. Um, you know, Titus for his eyes, he's a great athlete. You know, a lot a lot of the guys on our offensive line can move and can run. So, I think, you know, this offense, you know, allows us to showcase that and puts us in a good light. >> It's true. Who's a better athlete, you or Spencer? [laughter] >> I mean, of course, I'm going to say I'm the better athlete, but [laughter] the numbers backing up. >> No, nobody wants to see penalties, but Todd has said before he despises >> football. How have you seen him sort of emphasize that out here on the practice field? Yeah, I mean we all hate penalties, you know, uh especially up front, you know, false starts, holding, you know, those things erase plays, erase explosives. So, you know, it's really on us to have that composure to, you know, stay on sides, to not hold, to, you know, do what we have to do to not erase those plays. But, you know, he's really emphasized that, you know, if we have a penalty out there, we're reloading the play. If you're false starting, you're coming out. Um, so it really, you know, forces that accountability onto you where it's like, okay, I'm coming out today. I got to be locked in to the snap count, um, to my technique so I'm not having penalties in practice. >> Some of these drills that are slower, maybe designed to just kind of show you guys how it's done, where to line up and stuff like that. Maybe not everyone's favorite part of practice, but how how important are those? >> That's important, too. Um, you know, I think a lot of guys realize it, too. A lot of these slower times, we're running the same plays we are during the faster times. So, you know, it gives you uh a chance to work through it slowly slowly so that when we're going faster, you already know what you're doing. You know what the count is, uh you know what the code word is that's going to come up in the, you know, faster period? >> Z, when you're not in the pads and hitting and going live this time of year, what what makes for a successful OTAA type of practice for for like the offensive line? >> Well, I think for us, you know, we have to have mastery of the playbook. We got to learn what our assignment is, what we have to do on every play. But second of all, we got to learn the the fundamentals and technique that are called for for this offense. Um, and that's really measured day-to-day by, you know, film study when we watch the tape. Um, what the tape looks like. Um, you know, how many times are you having mental errors? Are you running the wrong play? Are you off sides? I think that's how you measure it for us up front.

title: Exclusive Interview with Travis Switzer
text: Very happy now to be joined by Brown's offensive coordinator, Travis Schwitzer. And Travis, first open to the media session here of the OTAAS. Yesterday you guys had one as well. How's kind of things progressing and what' you see out there today? >> Uh yeah, I mean we certainly have uh a long way to go to get to where we want to be, but I mean the guys are making strides. Um we had a few cadence things. We added some cadence today. Um that's part of it too. You add cadence, there's going to be hiccups as you go through it, but you got to stay with it. If you really want it to be a weapon for you, then you got to stay with it and uh and stay true to it. How's it kind of been for you in this process? First time as an offensive coordinator, obviously with Todd coming from Baltimore, but being able to kind of install this thing and are you guys where you want to be, you know, at this early stage? Cuz >> it looks pretty I'll tell you what, from the sidelines, it looks pretty smooth out there. >> No, we're off to a good start. Like I said, we we got a long way to go and and we're going to get there, but we're off to a good start. The guys are doing a nice job. Um there's several guys that are making strides, uh learning a new system. We did get a chance to go through it in the vet mini camp a little bit and then also in phase two. So, this is now, you know, the second or third time with some of these installs, which is nice. You get get a little bit of repetitiveness. Um, you get to drill down on the details a little bit more, which really is what makes the game go. >> I love the pace of practice. I mean, it feels like we are getting a lot of work in these practices. Is that something you guys are being, you know, very intentional about making sure we maximize every second that we've got? >> No, I think so. And I think we'd like it faster, to be honest. So, that's something we'll grow to. But, yeah, I mean, the idea is if you get out here and you practice fast, the game feels easy, you know, compared to what you do every day. What do you want the identity of this offense to be? >> Uh that that's a that's a wide question. Um we want to play the game on our terms. So you need to be multiple in order to do that. You need to be able to run the football and you need to be able to protect the passer number one and you got to take care of the ball, you know. So play play the game on our terms uh not on the defenses. >> Let's talk about the quarterbacks now because we got to see both Deshan and Shador get some time with the ones as well today. How have they done it? It's a new system for all those guys in that room. How have they done kind of picking things up and taking it out here onto the field? They're doing a great job and we're carrying things over from the meeting to our walkthrough sessions over to the field. They're really doing a good job at the line of scrimmage. Owning the line of scrimmage very important for the quarterback is number one job. Um and then also just giving them a little bit more freedom too. Uh and they're really taking that they're taking that uh that seriously and I think they want that which is awesome. >> That gives them some ownership of the offense. And for the people listening when you say giving them some freedom, what does that mean? Uh yeah. I mean whether you're calling two plays in the huddle and they're changing it or they're changing it on their own. Um there's communication, you know, on every play. Yeah. Um and the more that they're thinking that way, you know, the better off we're going to be >> because then that's kind of making them say, "Okay, what do I see here? What do I like against what I see here?" And let's get into that, >> right? Yeah. Otherwise, you're guessing, you know, so it's better if they can do it. >> Yeah. All right. All right. I want to ask you about one of the the periods that you guys had here today, which is something I hadn't seen before where it was kind of line up full speed, snap the ball, and as soon as it snap, the whistle's blown dead. What what's the point of the of those? >> Yeah, it's our perfect operation period. So, the idea is we're going to emphasize everything until the snap, basically. So, we're in and out of the huddle. Coach Monk talks about the four twos all the time, right? We're trying to save 8 seconds between every uh play call, right? So, that's getting the call in 2 seconds faster. That's getting in the huddle 2 seconds faster. It's shortening the call so that when we're in the huddle, we we get out 2 seconds faster and then it's sprinting to the ball and getting lined up. Anytime you have a decision maker, you're trying to relieve anxiety. You know, I mean, he used this analogy all the time like if you were getting operated on, you wouldn't want the doctor to be rushing in there sweating, you know, looking like he's rough. We assess the situation. >> Yeah. We'd like to save some time and relieve anxiety for any decision maker, and the quarterback is certainly one of those. >> Yeah. One of the things with the rules as well is you have for a certain period of time, you're still able to talk to them into their their helmet. So it'd be like having the super surgeon talking to the surgeon and saying, "Hey, let's make sure we do this." Right? So that's it's all important to be able to dis because so much of the league now is disguise and reaction, but if you can kind of get to the point where you see what you're doing, get your check, they're going to check that allows you to kind of check check check, keep going till you have the advantage. >> Yeah. No, 100%. I mean, communication is everything with that. You know, we got to all be on the same page and know what we're doing. >> I saw you do a little bit on the side here with Quinn Sean and you had Dylan over there. Is that stuff that that's kind of the fun where you get the one-on-one kind of go through make sure everybody's on the same page, they understand all the different checks because it does sound like with that freedom comes a lot of checks for everybody involved on the offense as well. >> No doubt. And that goes back to the communication piece of it. Um I I I think that we organize it in in a in a pretty good way where everybody understands what we're looking for um on everything and and they can anticipate which helps. Um but the communication is is is the huge part of it. >> All right, let's talk about these young receivers. I got I was so excited on draft day bringing some young receivers. We wanted weapons here for a long time. You've had some of those in Baltimore. We needed to get some weapons here. You get Casey, you get Denzel obviously with the guys that we have. But highlight today was obviously Deshawn down there to Denzel. But how have those young guys done because that's going to be a big part. And Isaiah Bonsi, young guy as well who can run. What how are they kind of picking things up here is so that they can be playing fast. >> No question. I I think they're doing a great job. I mean, we saw the play here. I mean, he did he had a great one yesterday, too, where he held the red line. We just got to give him a better ball, give him a chance. But, um, yeah, that's that's really encouraging to see both those guys doing a great job. Is it fun to have Todd talk about different styles right at that position and you think of a guy like Casey and I think what's so cool about him the way he doesn't even move his shoulders when he can come in and out of brakes and then you got big bodied guy and Denzel you got speed and Isaiah you got Judy who's been a pro bowler you got big said Tilman is that kind of fun in terms of when you put it together we have a lot of different tools that we can use and body body styles body types depending on what matches up the best for our opponents just allows you talked about being multiple right >> right no 100% I mean everybody in this building uh doesn't matter what time of year it is in The NFL has at least one elite trait, >> you know, so we're trying to put all those together. We're going to work on everything, right? I want the best for, >> you know, anybody in this world to have a great life. I think it's really cool that he still has an opportunity with a change, right, to showcase his ability, see where he's at. I'm all for it. >> Todd, a question about your schedule. You have worked in Jacksonville and Tampa, so you know what's waiting for you in September weatherwise. Has that affected your training camp plans at all? >> No, I think it's awesome. I think it's a great start. I think for us it's a I wouldn't want it any more better than that. I mean, should we get to go down to Florida? Certainly a team that a year ago was in a similar spot as we are, you know, where are they going from there? And a team that was a playoff team and really had every opportunity to beat the Bills at home and didn't. But I'm excited. Playoff team in Florida, 10 something degrees, middle of the day, and if that doesn't get you fired up, that didn't get our guys fired up for the offseason, then go to training camp, I don't know what will. Todd, you've known about Deshawn's athleticism for a long time. And before you got here, you probably didn't know how driven he was. What does it say about him that he still wants to be an elite player after all he's been through over the last couple years? >> Oh, I think it's really cool. I know I've said that like five times today, but like here's a guy that really at this point has made plenty of money. I think we all know that, right? [clears throat] He's had plenty of success and has has has had disappointment, you know, in his career. A number of things he couldn't control from an injury standpoint. But to come back and want to battle, want to um further his career and change the narrative, I think it's really cool. >> Do you feel like the quarterbacks are all bringing out the best in each other? and you see the competition kind of elevating. >> I don't know that. You'd have to ask those guys if that's what motivates them. I don't I don't know that. I would guess that just the idea of the opportunity to be the starter for the Cleveland Browns, one of 32 teams in the NFL is enough. But um I don't know that. You'd have to ask them that. >> Just for the record, have you had any face to face with Garrett yet? >> Miles? >> Yeah. some of the some of the slower walkthrough stuff you guys to guys do at the start practice to get organized. How important is that? It seems like a small thing, but how important is that in the in the big picture to help >> Well, you can't beat your guys into the ground. So, it's about getting reps. So, the the start of practice, you know, being more of a jog through allows you to buy some reps and allows you to do more two spot. the more you uh you know you slow the tempo down, the more you can divide your guys up and that allows you to get you know more opportunity for guys to learn and develop. So that's an integral part of what we'll do now and as long as I'm still here. >> Todd, um last one going back you've had a lot of experience in in college especially, you know, most recently at Georgia. How much has that college experience helped with when you're in this stage of, you know, offseason training camp when you have the roster's 90, you have a lot of players, you're you're trying to evaluate. How much is that college experience and how you deal with the massive the large rosters helped in terms of dealing with what you deal with, you know, setting things up here for that evaluation? >> It helps. I mean, you're used to having a bigger roster in college. Obviously, it's shrunk now, so you're used to you know, in terms of going more spot, trying to find more reps, more walkth through. Now, the rules hinder that a little bit because the moment we get on the field, you have two hours. I mean, that's what you've got. So, uh, minus any type of, you know, stretching or all that stuff, but you're up against it a little bit where when you get mini camps or training camp, it's not the same. But certainly being in college and having a bigger roster and forcing yourself to rep all those players and and we're in the development business. I mean, let's not kid ourselves what what business we're in. I mean, you don't get 15 first round picks. You don't get that. You get the picks you get and you've got to develop everybody on your roster and eventually the guys that make your team and your practice squad, they're all going to play at some point. So, I think it's uh imperative that we get as many reps as we can within the constraints that that we have.

title: Mason Graham Press Conference | May 20th, 2026
text: This is it is your second year so that that difference but with the new coordinator does it feel any different? I mean just a little tweaks here and there you know every coordinator wants to put a little twist on you know their defense but really wanted to keep it mostly the same for the front so we're kind of just sticking with our plan and attacking getting penetration disrupting. So the tweaks aren't affecting you as much. No I mean every defense like there's movement and different places but you know everyone kind of runs similar schemes nowadays and similar blitzes so just good football. I feel like he's a player's coach you know he just wants to be around the guys he wants to us to talk to him like he's another one of us on the field so I really like his energy brings a lot of juice um to defense and you know I feel like that's a good thing for us. A year ago you were talking about learning to play you know take the handcuffs off I believe was the phrase you paraphrasing How much more comfortable you just feel like in the kind of aggressive attacking front you're playing in now compared to you know what you were you played in at Michigan. As you Oh yeah I broke a rib so I mean it hurt pretty bad just take a little pill before the game suck it up a little bit and get through it. I mean what's the toughest part dealing with I mean obviously I know you can't sleep it's hard to breathe all that stuff what's the toughest Yeah I mean just you know especially for linemen you know getting hit by you know if I'm over here hitting this guy you know someone can come hit me on my side where my ribs are but you know I just you know I took the chance of playing so I wasn't really thinking about it in the moment but definitely felt it after the games. Can you make any observation about Fana and Brailsford at all? I don't know how much you Nah. I don't think I can make like an uh you know, I think they see pads and you know, training camp and all that stuff. Obviously, no pads, no contact right now but the defense looks really aggressive today. Is that something that you guys have made a mental note to do to come out aggressively and and what do you think this identity of the defense can be if you're already making plays in in OTAs right now? I mean, yeah, it's the goal, you know, just to you know, be the better side of the ball at the end of the day, you know, I feel like you know, in my opinion, you know, offense got the better of us yesterday so I feel like we kind of pushed back today and kind of you know, reestablished ourselves but we're just going to keep getting better as a team and defense really. Do you remember Do you remember when you broke that rib? Uh Who did we play before Tennessee? It was San Francisco. Yeah, San Francisco I broke San Francisco I cracked it and then Tennessee game I made a play like the first or second play I made a tackle and I broke it all the way and I just kind of just played through that. I kind of knew what it was. Speaking of San Francisco, that was the game where Malik suffered the injury. You guys had really sort of it seemed like really established a nice kind of one-two punch inside. How much did you notice a difference in the way teams were attacking you and approaching you after Malik left the lineup and and how good is it to off of that, how good is it to have Malik back this year, you know, alongside? Yeah, I mean, I feel like it you know, it wasn't too much of a difference, you know, obviously, you know, they I would say they paid more attention to Malik and Miles when they were both in so it was kind of and then me and Alex so but I feel like when Malik went kind of went down it was kind of you know, me and Miles now and they kind of took on that role but you know, we're just trying to rush four as one. You know, we're trying to work together as we rush and you know, I'm looking forward to you know, when Malik comes back. I've been talking to him. I know he's getting better and working hard, so I know a lot of your impact doesn't show up on the stat sheet necessarily, but when when you kind of look back on last year, do you feel like you left some some plays out there or what more could you have done last year defensively? Yeah, I feel like there's always plays, you know, you know, you feel like you can make or you want back in a sense, but you know, it is what it is. You know, I'm just working on just improving this year. You know, that year is in the past. Just kind of watch my I'll watch my tape, reevaluated myself, and you know, kind of just worked on some things this off-season. Just kind of want to take more steps this season. What have you noticed about Monken's approach to especially this time of year in practice versus maybe what you kind of experienced in year one and then how do you think it's going to prepare you guys for for next season? Uh I know he's from that Raven's tree. You know, I played for Harbaugh, so I feel like there's kind of a similar resemblance there, you know, all about hard work. He wants to get a lot of plays, um and he I feel like you know, I I think I think like him, too. You know, I feel like the best way of getting good at football is playing football and getting reps, so that's what I like. What has the off-season experience been like for you not having to to worry about being drafted or not worrying about anything like like you're going into a couple years in this season. What what's the off-season experience been like for you? I feel like it's just been more smooth, you know, I've had more time to you know, work on the things I wanted to like getting stronger. Um I was training in Dallas, you know, had a good few months there and then you know, just hit the ground running when I came back with all the other guys and started doing I feel like there's just more I had more time to you know, work on my stuff rather than you know, meeting with teams and doing combine stuff and all that, so Do you understand why Garrett's not here or do you wonder why he's not here? I mean, he's the best player in the NFL, so I'm not taking any way from him not showing up. I know he's got his own life and you know, he's just a different individual, but you know, I know come time on Sunday he's going to be ready to work.
